title: Assistant Temporal Survey Officer
summary: Support the continuous watch over indicators of temporal imbalance in Wales and, where directed, associated jurisdictions.
duties: Attend reported Excess Time Events under the supervision of a Continuity Inspector.
Complete field logs to the standard set out in DET-MANUAL-003.
Preserve accurate and impartial records of all recognised events.
Do not interpret causes. Record consequences.
essential: Right to work in the United Kingdom.
A full UK driving licence, or the ability to travel independently across Wales.
Accuracy in written English. Welsh is desirable.
The ability to apply a published procedure without improving it.
desirable: Experience of operational casework in a public body.

title: Archive Conservator
summary: Conserve paper, film and instrument records of Excess Time Events. Contradiction is retained. It is not resolved.
duties: Assess, treat and house holdings of the Institute for Temporal Studies.
Maintain the retention schedule DET-RET-011.
Prepare material for authorised research access.
Report deterioration that cannot be explained by ordinary ageing.
essential: A recognised qualification in archive conservation or equivalent experience.
Right to work in the United Kingdom.
Experience of working to BS 4971 or an equivalent standard.
desirable: Experience of film or instrument collections.

title: Continuity Inspector
hours: 37 hours a week, unsocial hours as required
summary: Inspect sites at which measurable continuity has diverged from ordinary expectation and produced demonstrable effects upon public life.
duties: Lead the departmental response to a recognised Excess Time Event.
Determine whether restoration is reasonably practicable.
Issue and vary notices under the operational procedures.
Give evidence to the Minister as required.
essential: Substantial experience of inspection, regulation or emergency coordination in a public body.
Right to work in the United Kingdom.
A full UK driving licence.
The ability to write a decision letter that a court could read.
desirable: Experience of working with local authorities and emergency services.

title: Senior Drift Analyst
summary: Lead the measurement of temporal drift and the preparation of the National Risk Register entry for Excess Time.
duties: Own the statistical yearbook and the quarterly drift tables.
Advise the Institute for Temporal Studies on method.
Ensure that coincidence is not recorded as explanation.
Brief the Minister and the Permanent Secretary.
essential: A degree in a quantitative discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
Experience of official statistics or a comparable published series.
Right to work in the United Kingdom.
desirable: Experience of the Government Statistical Service.

title: Records Officer (Information Rights)
summary: Administer freedom of information, subject access and the temporal records that those regimes do not quite cover.
duties: Log and answer requests under FOIA, GDPR and DET-GDPR-001.
Apply exemptions where the record is of an event that has not yet become eligible.
Maintain the disclosure log.
Do not confirm or deny holdings that would themselves constitute an Excess Time Event.
essential: Experience of information rights or casework administration.
Right to work in the United Kingdom.
Accuracy under statutory deadlines.

title: Community Programmes Officer
summary: Deliver the community programmes through which the Department reduces harm arising from temporal displacement wherever reasonably practicable.
duties: Administer grants and local agreements under DET-COM-012.
Work with local authorities and community groups.
Report outcomes without claiming that ordinary life has been improved.
Keep the public assurance: most citizens will never knowingly encounter an event.
essential: Experience of community or grant programmes in the public or voluntary sector.
Right to work in the United Kingdom.
The ability to travel in Wales.

title: Welsh Language Officer
summary: Own the Welsh language scheme DET-WELSH-001 and the bilingual standard of departmental publishing.
duties: Advise on translation of operational notices and public guidance.
Monitor compliance with the Welsh Language Standards as they apply to the Department.
The Codex is issued in English. Supporting material is not excused.
essential: Welsh and English to professional standard.
Right to work in the United Kingdom.
Experience of bilingual public-sector publishing.

title: Apprentice Records Assistant
summary: A first post in the public register of Excess Time Events. You will not be asked to hold a case alone.
duties: File, retrieve and paginate records under supervision.
Learn DET-MANUAL-003 and the forms catalogue.
Attend the civic induction and the Institute reading room as required.
essential: Age 16 or over on the day you start.
Right to work in the United Kingdom.
GCSE English, or equivalent, at grade C/4 or above.
desirable: An interest in archives or public administration.
